name: Berberis

study_strategy.warning: B. trifoliolata and B. swaseyi hybridize in Central Texas. Leaflet count alone can misidentify hybrids.

quick_split: B. trifoliolata — usually 3 stiff holly-like leaflets; dense rounded agarita habit.
B. swaseyi — usually 5–9 leaflets, reduced basal pair, duller reticulate foliage; more open Edwards Plateau shrub.
B. aquifolium — many pinnate holly-like leaflets + blue-purple berries; non-native Texas comparison.
comparison_lesson.caveat: Use leaflet architecture plus bracts/surface texture for suspected hybrids.

shared_genus_traits: Evergreen woody shrubs with stiff spine-tipped leaflets and yellow flowers.
Flowers have petaloid sepals, six nectar-bearing petals and six stamens; fruits are berries.
look_here_first: Examine an intact compound leaf including its rachis base. Count leaflets, check for a reduced basal pair, then compare upper and lower leaflet surfaces. Use floral structures to confirm the genus; treat mixed parental traits as possible hybrid material.

species_comparison_matrix.swaseyi: Usually 5–9 leaflets, often with a reduced basal pair
species_comparison_matrix.aquifolium: Many pinnate holly-like leaflets; nursery comparison

species_comparison_matrix.swaseyi: Dull gray-green, strongly reticulate, often pale underside
Often more open, but can be low and dense

overlap_and_cautions: B. trifoliolata and B. swaseyi hybridize; intermediates may have 5–7 leaflets, so count alone is not conclusive.
Inspect multiple intact mature leaves, especially the basal pair, before assigning a parent species.
Flower-bract distinctions need a verified key before being used as a definitive hybrid discriminator.
B. aquifolium remains a non-Texas-native comparison, not a native-range PASS.

local_lookalikes.name: Berberis hybrid intermediate
local_lookalikes.distinction: Conflicting leaflet count, reduced basal pair and surface texture; retain intermediate uncertainty.

local_lookalikes.name: Ilex spp.
local_lookalikes.distinction: Inspect whether leaves are simple rather than pinnately compound.

local_lookalikes.name: Nandina domestica
local_lookalikes.distinction: More divided foliage and longitudinal anther opening rather than Berberis hinged valves.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: Matched intact leaves of all three species, including rachis and basal leaflet attachments.
Matched leaf undersides and upper surfaces showing reticulate veins and glaucous coating.
Same-scale flower and bract close-ups of both Central Texas species and suspected intermediates.
Matched fully ripe berries, recording maturity and attachment.
Label existing saved Joey footage frames for B. trifoliolata leaflets and B. swaseyi leaflets/abaxial surface; private study only.

targeted_handoff.question: Verify a bract-based and leaf-venation hybrid key for B. trifoliolata versus B. swaseyi before teaching firm thresholds; do not reopen range status.
